exposure.statement: Chocolate products contributed 4.3% of cadmium dietary exposure across age groups (FoodEx detailed categories; lower bound).

High cadmium levels found in algal formulations, cocoa-based products, crustaceans, edible offal, fungi, oilseeds, seaweeds and water molluscs; cocoa powder and bitter/bitter-sweet chocolate among 13 categories with MB mean >100 µg/kg; cocoa powder and chocolate products among categories with individual results >=1,000 µg/kg.

Within 'Sugar and confectionary', chocolate (cocoa) products account for the following share of that category's LB exposure: infants 15.3%, toddlers 81.3%, other children 87.2%, adolescents 92.2%, adults 90.8%, elderly 86.0%, very elderly 88.7%.

Within 'Vegetables and vegetable products', cocoa beans and cocoa products account for: infants 0.5%, toddlers 3.7%, other children 23.7%, adolescents 25.5%, adults 3.6%, elderly 1.6%, very elderly 1.9% of that category's LB exposure.
Within 'Non-alcoholic beverages', cocoa beverage accounts for: toddlers 0.7%, other children 4.3%, adolescents 11.3%, adults 2.7%, elderly 1.3%, very elderly 1.5% of that category's LB exposure.
Chocolate (cocoa) products ranked 6th contributor to LB Cd exposure in toddlers.
Other children: chocolate (cocoa) products ranked 3rd (6.39%) and cocoa beans and cocoa products 7th (3.00%); together close to 10% of exposure.
Adolescents: chocolate (cocoa) products ranked 4th (5.88%) and cocoa beans and cocoa products 8th (3.30%).
Elderly: chocolate (cocoa) products ranked 14th; chocolate decreased considerably in the elderly.

Chocolate products, especially dark chocolate, are the main drivers of exposure from sugar and confectionary; cocoa beans and cocoa products peaked in older children and adolescents within vegetables.
EFSA CONTAM TWI for cadmium (JECFA PTMI 25 µg/kg bw noted for comparison).
Middle-bound lifetime average weekly exposure 2.04 µg/kg bw; potential P95 3.66 µg/kg bw.

contradictions_with_stored_summary: Stored summary table lists Chocolate n=1,286 at 80.1/80.9/81.8 without noting that this is the Level 2 remainder after bitter, bitter-sweet and milk chocolate Level 3 rows were split out (combined n=1,558). Otherwise values match the primary.
unresolved: Only means (LB/MB/UB) printed; no medians/P95/ranges for cocoa or chocolate.
Per-food left-censoring proportion not printed; only FoodEx Level 1 aggregates.
Cocoa powder n=732 is identical to JECFA 91 WHO European Region cocoa powder n=732 (mean 228 there vs 183 here); likely the same records treated differently - duplication risk across sources.
